subproblems.statement: Let Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ be open and u : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q locally Lipschitz on Ω. There are C¹ maps G_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q, open sets O_k ⊆ ℝⁿ and pairwise disjoint Borel sets E_k ⊆ O_k ∩ Ω (k ∈ ℕ) such that each G_k is antilipschitz on O_k (c_k|w − w′| ≤ |G_k(w) − G_k(w′)| for w, w′ ∈ O_k, some c_k > 0), u(w) = G_k(w) and u has Fréchet derivative DG_k(w) at every w ∈ E_k, and Lⁿ-almost every w ∈ Ω at which u is differentiable with injective derivative belongs to ⋃_k E_k.

Conventions used below. ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure; on ℝⁿ it equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume, it is invariant under isometries and translations and scales by λⁿ under x ↦ λx). An n-covector α is a continuous alternating n-linear map (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm ‖α‖ (least C with |α(u₁,…,u_n)| ≤ C Π|u_i|); an n-vector is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors with the operator norm; simpleNVector v is the n-vector α ↦ α(v₁,…,v_n), so |simpleNVector v (α)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π|v_i|; for a linear map A, A_# w := nVectorPushforward n A w = w ∘ A^#, where A^#α = α(A·,…,A·), it is linear in w and A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A v) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`). A map Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This lemma packages the C¹ Approximation Theorem (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5, printed proof copied in step 3) and the local inverse function theorem argument used in the parent proof (Step 5.2) and in Simon's proof of Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2. Let Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ be open and u : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q locally Lipschitz on Ω. Write R := {w ∈ Ω : u is differentiable at w with injective derivative}.

1. (Case n = 0.) ℝ⁰ = {0}. If Ω = ∅ take G_k :≡ 0, O_k := ∅, E_k := ∅ for all k (all clauses hold vacuously; the antilipschitz clause with c = 1). If Ω = {0} take G_0 :≡ u(0) (constant, C¹), O_0 := ℝ⁰, E_0 := {0}, and G_k :≡ 0, O_k := ∅, E_k := ∅ for k ≥ 1. Every map on the one-point space has derivative 0 at 0 and fderiv of a constant is 0, so u(0) = G_0(0) and HasFDerivAt u (fderiv G_0 0) 0; the antilipschitz inequality is 0 ≤ … on ℝ⁰; and 0 ∈ E_0. From now on n ≥ 1 (the argument below also works for n = 0).

2. (Reduction to globally Lipschitz maps.) For each w ∈ Ω there is r > 0 with B_r(w) ⊆ Ω and u Lipschitz on B_r(w) (Ω open, u locally Lipschitz on Ω). Let B_1, B_2, … enumerate the open balls with rational centre and rational radius that are contained in Ω and on which u is Lipschitz; they cover Ω (every w lies in a rational ball inside its B_r(w)). For each m let u_m : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q be a Lipschitz extension of u|B_m (componentwise McShane extension; `LipschitzOnWith.extend_pi` composed with a linear isomorphism ℝ^Q ≅ (Fin Q → ℝ), or SimonGMT `exists_lipschitz_extension_finiteDimensional`). Then u = u_m on the open set B_m.

3. (C¹ Approximation Theorem, Simon Ch. 2, 1.5; printed proof.) Claim: if g : ℝⁿ → ℝ is Lipschitz and ε > 0, there are a closed set A ⊆ ℝⁿ with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ A) < ε and h ∈ C¹(ℝⁿ) such that at every x ∈ A, g is differentiable, g(x) = h(x) and ∇g(x) = ∇h(x).
 Proof (Simon): By Rademacher's theorem (Simon Ch. 2, 1.4; SimonGMT `rademacher_ae_differentiableAt`) g is differentiable on a Borel set D with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ D) = 0, and ∇g is Borel measurable (Mathlib `measurable_fderiv`). By Lusin's theorem (valid for Lⁿ on ℝⁿ, a σ-finite Radon measure) there is a closed C₀ with ∇g|C₀ continuous and Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ C₀) < ε/4, and by inner regularity of Lⁿ there is a closed F ⊆ D with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ F) < ε/4 (Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ D) = 0); C := C₀ ∩ F is closed, C ⊆ D, ∇g|C is continuous and Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ C) < ε/2. For x, y ∈ C, x ≠ y, put R(x,y) := (g(y) − g(x) − ∇g(x)·(y − x))/|x − y|, and for k ≥ 1 put η_k(x) := sup{|R(x,y)| : y ∈ C, 0 < |y − x| < 1/k} (≤ 2 Lip g). For fixed y, x ↦ R(x,y) is continuous on C ∖ {y}, so η_k is lower semicontinuous on C, hence Borel; η_k ↓ 0 pointwise on C because g is differentiable at each x ∈ C. By Egoroff's theorem applied to the finite-measure sets C ∩ (B_j(0) ∖ B_{j−1}(0)) with tolerances ε/2^{j+3}, there is a measurable A₀ ⊆ C with Lⁿ(C ∖ A₀) < ε/4 such that η_k → 0 uniformly on each bounded subset of A₀. Choose a closed A ⊆ A₀ with Lⁿ(A₀ ∖ A) < ε/4. Then Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ A) < ε, g|A and ∇g|A are continuous, and for each compact K ⊆ A: for x ∈ K, y ∈ A, 0 < |y − x| < 1/k we have |R(x,y)| ≤ η_k(x) ≤ sup_K η_k → 0, i.e. R(x,y) → 0 as y → x in A uniformly for x ∈ K. This is hypothesis (‡) of the Whitney Extension Theorem (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.6; see [EG92, §6.5], [Fed69, 3.1.14]; partial Lean machinery: SimonGMT `HasWhitneyC1Compatibility.hasFDerivAt_whitneyExtension` in Chapter02/WhitneyExtension.lean), which yields h ∈ C¹(ℝⁿ) with h = g and ∇h = ∇g on A. At x ∈ A ⊆ D, g is differentiable. □
 Apply the claim to each component u_m^l (l = 1,…,Q) with ε := 1/(i·max(Q,1)) and intersect the Q closed sets (if Q = 0 take A_{m,i} := ℝⁿ and G_{m,i} :≡ 0; every map into ℝ⁰ is differentiable with derivative 0): for every m and i ≥ 1 there are a closed A_{m,i} with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ A_{m,i}) < 1/i and G_{m,i} ∈ C¹(ℝⁿ;ℝ^Q) such that at every w ∈ A_{m,i}: u_m is differentiable (all components are), u_m(w) = G_{m,i}(w) and Du_m(w) = DG_{m,i}(w).

4. (Covering of R.) Let w ∈ R ∩ B_m. As u = u_m on the open set B_m, u_m is differentiable at w with Du_m(w) = Du(w), which is injective. So R ∩ B_m ∖ ⋃_i A_{m,i} ⊆ ⋂_i (ℝⁿ ∖ A_{m,i}), which has measure ≤ 1/i for every i, hence is Lⁿ-null. Put D_{m,i} := {w ∈ B_m ∩ A_{m,i} : DG_{m,i}(w) is injective}. For w ∈ R ∩ B_m ∩ A_{m,i} we have DG_{m,i}(w) = Du_m(w) = Du(w) injective, so w ∈ D_{m,i}. Since R ⊆ ⋃_m B_m, we get Lⁿ(R ∖ ⋃_{m,i} D_{m,i}) = 0. Each D_{m,i} is Borel: B_m is open, A_{m,i} is closed, and {w : DG_{m,i}(w) injective} is open (DG_{m,i} is continuous and injectivity of a linear map ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q is an open condition, being equivalent to min_{|s|=1}|As| > 0).

5. (Local antilipschitz property — inverse function theorem argument.) Let w ∈ D_{m,i}, G := G_{m,i}, A := DG(w) and c := ½ min_{|s|=1} |As| > 0. By continuity of DG there is r > 0 with ‖DG(z) − DG(w)‖ ≤ c for |z − w| < r. For z, z′ ∈ B_r(w) (a convex set), the mean value inequality applied to z ↦ G(z) − Az gives |G(z) − G(z′) − A(z − z′)| ≤ c|z − z′|, hence |G(z) − G(z′)| ≥ |A(z − z′)| − c|z − z′| ≥ 2c|z − z′| − c|z − z′| = c|z − z′|. So G is c-antilipschitz on B_r(w), hence on every rational ball O with w ∈ O ⊆ B_r(w) ∩ B_m (such O exists). Let 𝒪_{m,i} be the countable set of rational open balls O ⊆ B_m on which G_{m,i} is c-antilipschitz for some c > 0; then D_{m,i} ⊆ ⋃_{O ∈ 𝒪_{m,i}} O.

6. (The pieces.) Enumerate the countable set of triples (m, i, O) with O ∈ 𝒪_{m,i} as k = 0, 1, 2, … (pad with G_k :≡ 0, O_k := ∅, E′_k := ∅ if it is finite), and set G_k := G_{m,i}, O_k := O, E′_k := D_{m,i} ∩ O, and finally E_k := E′_k ∖ ⋃_{l<k} E′_l. Verification:
 • O_k is open; G_k is C¹ (`ContDiff ℝ 1`); G_k is antilipschitz on O_k with some c > 0 (definition of 𝒪_{m,i}).
 • E_k is Borel (step 4), E_k ⊆ O ⊆ B_m ⊆ Ω, so E_k ⊆ O_k ∩ Ω; the E_k are pairwise disjoint by construction.
 • For w ∈ E_k ⊆ B_m ∩ A_{m,i}: u(w) = u_m(w) = G_k(w); and since u = u_m on the open set B_m ∋ w and u_m is differentiable at w with Du_m(w) = DG_k(w) = fderiv ℝ G_k w, we get HasFDerivAt u (fderiv ℝ G_k w) w.
 • ⋃_k E_k = ⋃_k E′_k = ⋃_{m,i} D_{m,i} (each w ∈ D_{m,i} lies in some O ∈ 𝒪_{m,i}). By step 4, Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ Ω at which u is differentiable with injective derivative (i.e. w ∈ R) lies in ⋃_k E_k. This is the last clause, stated with `volume` = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ. ∎

Conventions. ℝᵏ = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with Euclidean norm |·|. Hⁿ = μHE[n], and on ℝⁿ we have Hⁿ = Lⁿ = volume (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Source. This is Step 1 of the proof of slicing_im_st_chart_data, i.e. Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 'only if' and Remark 1.3. The printed proof uses the C¹ Approximation Theorem (Ch. 2, 1.5), Lipschitz images of null sets, the area formula on the critical set, and local embeddings near noncritical points. Sub-steps (i) (C¹ approximation) and (iii) (antilipschitz estimate near points with injective derivative) of that Step 1 are packaged in the sibling lipschitz_c1_immersion_pieces (Submission.lpf_lipschitz_c1_immersion_pieces). Sub-step (ii) (null critical images) is the area formula in step 3 below, and sub-step (iv) (enumeration) is steps 6–8.

The sibling lipschitz_c1_immersion_pieces states the following. Let Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ be open and u : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q locally Lipschitz on Ω. Then there are C¹ maps G_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q, open sets O_k ⊆ ℝⁿ and pairwise disjoint Borel sets E_k ⊆ O_k ∩ Ω (k ∈ ℕ) with these properties:
- each G_k is c_k-antilipschitz on O_k for some c_k > 0;
- u(w) = G_k(w) and u has Fréchet derivative DG_k(w) at every w ∈ E_k;
- Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ Ω at which u has an injective Fréchet derivative lies in ⋃_k E_k.

Let M ⊆ ℝ^P be countably n-rectifiable.

1. (Unpacking Simon Ch. 3, 1.1.) By the definition (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable) there are M₀ ⊆ ℝ^P with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and maps F_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P (j ∈ ℕ) such that M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ) and each F_j is K_j-Lipschitz for some K_j ≥ 0.

2. (The sibling lemma.) Fix j. The set ℝⁿ is open, and F_j, being Lipschitz, is locally Lipschitz on ℝⁿ. Apply lipschitz_c1_immersion_pieces with Ω := ℝⁿ, Q := P and u := F_j. For k ∈ ℕ this gives C¹ maps G_{j,k} : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, open sets O_{j,k} ⊆ ℝⁿ and sets E_{j,k} ⊆ O_{j,k} such that:
   (a) G_{j,k} is c_{j,k}-antilipschitz on O_{j,k} for some c_{j,k} > 0;
   (b) F_j(w) = G_{j,k}(w) for every w ∈ E_{j,k};
   (c) for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ ℝⁿ: if F_j has at w a Fréchet derivative D that is injective, then w ∈ ⋃_k E_{j,k}.
   The remaining conclusions of the sibling (Borel sets E_{j,k}, pairwise disjoint, with derivative information on E_{j,k}) are not needed.

3. (Images of the non-regular points are Hⁿ-null; Rademacher and the area formula.) Let R_j := {w ∈ ℝⁿ : F_j is differentiable at w and DF_j(w) is injective}. We claim Hⁿ(F_j(ℝⁿ ∖ R_j)) = 0. Write ℝⁿ ∖ R_j = N_j ∪ C_j, where N_j := {w : F_j is not differentiable at w} and C_j := {w : F_j is differentiable at w and DF_j(w) is not injective}.
   - By Rademacher's theorem (Simon Ch. 2, 1.4), Lⁿ(N_j) = 0. Since F_j is K_j-Lipschitz, Hⁿ(F_j(N_j)) ≤ K_jⁿ·Hⁿ(N_j) = K_jⁿ·Lⁿ(N_j) = 0.
   - By the area formula (Simon Ch. 2, §3), Hⁿ(F_j(C_j)) ≤ ∫_{C_j} JF_j dLⁿ = 0. The Jacobian JF_j = √det(DF_j*DF_j) vanishes exactly where DF_j is not injective.
   - Hence Hⁿ(F_j(ℝⁿ ∖ R_j)) ≤ Hⁿ(F_j(N_j)) + Hⁿ(F_j(C_j)) = 0.
   - (For n = 0, ℝ⁰ = {0} and R_j = ℝ⁰: every map on a one-point space is differentiable with derivative 0, which is injective on ℝ⁰. So the claim is trivial.)
   - In Lean this is SimonGMT Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero, applied to the Lipschitz map F_j with s := ℝⁿ. Its set areaRegularSet F_j is R_j, and finrank ℝ ℝⁿ = n (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). It needs `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz` (a built SimonGMT module; such imports may be added to the Submission header, as accepted candidate f9637977 did for AreaDomain).

4. (Regular points missed by the pieces form a null set.) Let Z_j := R_j ∖ ⋃_k E_{j,k}.
   - Let w ∈ R_j. Then D := DF_j(w) is injective and F_j has Fréchet derivative D at w. So, by 2(c), if w ∉ ⋃_k E_{j,k}, then w lies in the Lⁿ-null exceptional set of 2(c).
   - Hence Z_j is contained in that null set, and Lⁿ(Z_j) = 0.
   - F_j is K_j-Lipschitz on Z_j, and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ. So Hⁿ(F_j(Z_j)) ≤ K_jⁿ·Hⁿ(Z_j) = K_jⁿ·Lⁿ(Z_j) = 0 (SimonGMT euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn).

5. (F_j(ℝⁿ) is covered by the pieces up to a null set.) We show F_j(ℝⁿ) ∖ ⋃_k G_{j,k}(O_{j,k}) ⊆ F_j(ℝⁿ ∖ R_j) ∪ F_j(Z_j).
   - Let y = F_j(w) with y ∉ ⋃_k G_{j,k}(O_{j,k}).
   - If w ∉ R_j, then y ∈ F_j(ℝⁿ ∖ R_j).
   - Suppose w ∈ R_j and w ∈ E_{j,k} for some k. Then w ∈ O_{j,k}, and y = F_j(w) = G_{j,k}(w) by 2(b), so y ∈ G_{j,k}(O_{j,k}). This is a contradiction.
   - So in the remaining case w ∈ Z_j, and y ∈ F_j(Z_j).
   By steps 3 and 4, Hⁿ(F_j(ℝⁿ) ∖ ⋃_k G_{j,k}(O_{j,k})) = 0.

6. (C¹ maps are Lipschitz on balls.) Let Ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be C¹ and r ∈ ℝ.
   - DΨ is continuous, so it is bounded on the compact set B̄(0, r) by some C ≥ 0.
   - The open ball B(0, r) is convex, contained in B̄(0, r), and Ψ is differentiable there. By the mean value inequality (Convex.lipschitzOnWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le), Ψ is C-Lipschitz on B(0, r).
   - If r ≤ 0 the ball is empty and the claim is trivial.

7. (The charts.) Fix a bijection e : ℕ → ℕ × ℕ × ℕ (e.g. the inverse of Denumerable.eqv). For l ∈ ℕ with e(l) = (j, k, r), put Φ_l := G_{j,k} and Ω_l := O_{j,k} ∩ B(0, r). Then:
   - Ω_l is open, as an intersection of two open sets;
   - Φ_l is C¹ (step 2);
   - Φ_l is Lipschitz on Ω_l ⊆ B(0, r), by step 6 applied to G_{j,k} and r;
   - Φ_l is c_{j,k}-antilipschitz on Ω_l ⊆ O_{j,k} with c_{j,k} > 0, by 2(a).

8. (Coverage.) We show M ∖ ⋃_l Φ_l(Ω_l) ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j (F_j(ℝⁿ) ∖ ⋃_k G_{j,k}(O_{j,k})).
   - Let x ∈ M with x ∉ ⋃_l Φ_l(Ω_l). By step 1, x ∈ M₀ or x ∈ F_j(ℝⁿ) for some j.
   - In the second case suppose x = G_{j,k}(w) with w ∈ O_{j,k} for some k. Choose r ∈ ℕ with |w| < r and put l := e⁻¹(j, k, r). Then w ∈ Ω_l and x = Φ_l(w), contradicting x ∉ ⋃_l Φ_l(Ω_l).
   - Hence x ∈ F_j(ℝⁿ) ∖ ⋃_k G_{j,k}(O_{j,k}).
   The right-hand side is a countable union of Hⁿ-null sets: Hⁿ(M₀) = 0, and step 5 for every j. By monotonicity and countable subadditivity, Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_l Φ_l(Ω_l)) = 0.

9. (Conclusion.) Steps 7 and 8 give the required C¹ maps Φ_l and open sets Ω_l: each Φ_l is Lipschitz on Ω_l, each Φ_l is c-antilipschitz on Ω_l for some c > 0, and Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_l Φ_l(Ω_l)) = 0. ∎

Sibling lipschitz_c1_immersion_pieces with Ω := ℝⁿ and u := F_j: C¹ maps G_{j,k}, c_{j,k}-antilipschitz on open O_{j,k}, with F_j = G_{j,k} on E_{j,k} ⊆ O_{j,k}; Lⁿ-a.e. point where F_j has an injective derivative lies in ⋃_k E_{j,k}.

M ∖ ⋃_l Φ_l(Ω_l) ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j (F_j(ℝⁿ) ∖ ⋃_k G_{j,k}(O_{j,k})), a countable union of Hⁿ-null sets.

--- Accepted proof (verbatim) ---

Notation. ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Euclidean norm |·|. Lⁿ = volume is Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ, a locally finite, weakly regular additive Haar measure. (ℝⁿ)* = L(ℝⁿ, ℝ) carries the operator norm ‖·‖. For x ∈ ℝⁿ let Dg(x) := fderiv ℝ g x ∈ (ℝⁿ)*; by Mathlib's convention Dg(x) = 0 where g is not differentiable. For y ≠ x let R(x,y) := (g(y) − g(x) − Dg(x)(y − x))/|y − x|.

Source. This is Simon, Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5 (C¹ Approximation Theorem), in the stronger form that Simon's printed proof (p. 44) actually establishes: a closed set A on which g is differentiable. Printed proof: “By Rademacher's Theorem f is differentiable on a set B ⊆ ℝⁿ with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ B) = 0. By Lusin's theorem (which applies to sets of infinite measure for Lⁿ) there is a closed set C ⊆ B such that ∇f|C is continuous and Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ C) < ε/2. On C we define h(x) = f(x), τ(x) = ∇f(x) and R(x,y) for x, y ∈ C is as defined in 1.6 (‡). Evidently (since C ⊆ B) we have lim_{y→x, y∈C} R(x,y) = 0 ∀ x ∈ C, but not necessarily uniformly with respect to x on compact subsets of C as in 1.6 (‡). We therefore proceed as follows. For each k = 1, 2, … let η_k(x) = sup{|R(x,y)| : y ∈ C ∩ B_{1/k}(x) ∖ {x}}. Then η_k ↓ 0 pointwise in C, and hence by Egoroff's Theorem (applied to the finite measure sets C ∩ B_j(0), j = 1, 2, …) there is an Lⁿ-measurable set A₀ ⊆ C such that Lⁿ(C ∖ A₀) < ε/4 and η_k converges uniformly to zero on each bounded subset of A₀. Since we can take a closed set A ⊆ A₀ with Lⁿ(A₀ ∖ A) < ε/4 we thus have Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ A) < ε and 1.6 (‡) holds. Hence we can apply the Whitney Theorem 1.6, and the proof is complete.”

The numbered proof below is this printed proof with every step filled in. The infinite-measure uses of Lusin's theorem and of closed inner approximation, and Egoroff's theorem, are all carried out on bounded open annuli.

1. (Reductions and annuli.)
- If ε > 1, in particular if ε = ∞, replace ε by 1: a set A with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ A) < 1 also has Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ A) < ε. So assume 0 < ε ≤ 1.
- Let S₁ := {x : |x| < 1} and S_j := {x : j − 1 < |x| < j} for j ≥ 2. The S_j are open, pairwise disjoint and bounded, so Lⁿ(S_j) < ∞.
- Z := ℝⁿ ∖ ⋃_j S_j = ⋃_{j≥1} {x : |x| = j} is a countable union of spheres of nonzero radius, so Lⁿ(Z) = 0 (Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.addHaar_sphere_of_ne_zero; for n = 0 these spheres are empty).
- Gluing fact (★), closedness: if F_j ⊆ S_j is closed for every j ≥ 1, then F := ⋃_j F_j is closed. The family (F_j) is locally finite, since the ball {|x| < r} meets S_j only if j − 1 < r (Mathlib LocallyFinite.isClosed_iUnion).
- Gluing fact (★), continuity: if a map φ is continuous on every F_j, then φ is continuous on F. Each x ∈ F_j has the open neighbourhood S_j with S_j ∩ F = F_j, because the S_l are pairwise disjoint. So near x the restriction of φ to F coincides with its restriction to F_j.

2. (Rademacher.) g is K-Lipschitz, so by Rademacher's theorem (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.4; Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt; SimonGMT rademacher_ae_differentiableAt) the set D := {x : g is differentiable at x} has Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ D) = 0. D is Borel (Mathlib measurableSet_of_differentiableAt), and x ↦ Dg(x) is Borel measurable (Mathlib measurable_fderiv). For x ∈ D we have ‖Dg(x)‖ ≤ K, because |Dg(x)v| = lim_{t→0} |g(x + tv) − g(x)|/|t| ≤ K|v| (Mathlib norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz).

3. (Lusin's theorem for Lⁿ on all of ℝⁿ.) Claim: there is a closed C ⊆ D such that Dg is continuous on C and Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ C) ≤ ε/4 < ε/2.
- Let e₁, …, e_n be the standard basis of ℝⁿ and fix j ≥ 1. S_j ∩ D is Borel and has finite measure.
- By inner regularity of Lⁿ by closed sets (Mathlib MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt) there is a closed F_j ⊆ S_j ∩ D with Lⁿ((S_j ∩ D) ∖ F_j) < ε/2^{j+3}.
- For l = 1, …, n the real function x ↦ Dg(x)e_l is Borel measurable. Lusin's theorem on the finite-measure set S_j ∩ D gives a closed C_{j,l} ⊆ S_j ∩ D with Lⁿ((S_j ∩ D) ∖ C_{j,l}) < ε/(2^{j+3}(n+1)) on which x ↦ Dg(x)e_l is continuous. Here Lusin is Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 1.17, i.e. SimonGMT Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable from the built module Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.Lusin, which must be imported explicitly. Its closed-inner-approximation hypothesis for Lⁿ is again MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt.
- Put C_j := F_j ∩ ⋂_{l=1}^{n} C_{j,l} (C_j = F_j if n = 0). Then C_j is closed and C_j ⊆ S_j ∩ D.
- Its measure defect is Lⁿ((S_j ∩ D) ∖ C_j) < ε/2^{j+3} + n·ε/(2^{j+3}(n+1)) < ε/2^{j+2}.
- Dg is continuous on C_j, because all its coordinates are: λ ↦ (λ(e₁), …, λ(e_n)) is a linear homeomorphism (ℝⁿ)* → ℝⁿ.
- Let C := ⋃_j C_j. By (★), C is closed and Dg is continuous on C; also C ⊆ D.
- Since ℝⁿ ∖ C ⊆ Z ∪ (ℝⁿ ∖ D) ∪ ⋃_j ((S_j ∩ D) ∖ C_j), we get Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ C) ≤ 0 + 0 + Σ_{j≥1} ε/2^{j+2} = ε/4.

4. (The functions η_k.) For k ≥ 1 and x ∈ C let η_k(x) := sup({|R(x,y)| : y ∈ C, 0 < |y − x| < 1/k} ∪ {0}); for x ∉ C let η_k(x) := 0.
(a) Bounds. For x ∈ C ⊆ D and y ≠ x, |R(x,y)| ≤ |g(y) − g(x)|/|y − x| + ‖Dg(x)‖ ≤ 2K. Hence 0 ≤ η_k ≤ 2K and η_k is real-valued.
(b) Convergence. η_{k+1} ≤ η_k, and η_k(x) → 0 for every x ∈ C. Given δ > 0, differentiability of g at x ∈ D gives ρ > 0 with |g(y) − g(x) − Dg(x)(y − x)| ≤ δ|y − x| whenever |y − x| < ρ. So η_k(x) ≤ δ once 1/k ≤ ρ.
(c) Measurability: η_k is Borel measurable.
- For fixed y ∈ C let φ_y : C → [0, ∞) be φ_y(x) := |R(x,y)| if 0 < |x − y| < 1/k, and φ_y(x) := 0 otherwise.
- φ_y is lower semicontinuous on C. The set U_y := {x ∈ C : 0 < |x − y| < 1/k} is relatively open in C, and φ_y is continuous on U_y: g is continuous, Dg is continuous on C by step 3, and |y − x| > 0 on U_y. This gives lower semicontinuity at points of U_y. At x₀ ∈ C ∖ U_y we have φ_y(x₀) = 0 ≤ φ_y(x) for all x ∈ C.
- As φ_y ≥ 0, η_k|C = sup_{y∈C} φ_y is a pointwise supremum of lower semicontinuous functions, hence lower semicontinuous on C.
- So each set {x ∈ C : η_k(x) > t} (t ∈ ℝ) is relatively open in the closed set C, hence Borel. Since η_k vanishes off C, η_k is Borel measurable on ℝⁿ.
- Equivalent route: if C′ ⊆ C is countable and dense in C, then η_k(x) = sup_{y∈C′} φ_y(x) for x ∈ C. This holds because y ↦ R(x,y) is continuous at every y ≠ x and the condition 0 < |y − x| < 1/k is open in y. So η_k is a countable supremum of Borel functions.

5. (Egoroff on bounded pieces.) Fix j ≥ 1.
- C_j = C ∩ S_j is Borel with Lⁿ(C_j) ≤ Lⁿ(S_j) < ∞. Every η_k is Borel measurable by 4(c), and η_k → 0 at every point of C_j by 4(b).
- By Egoroff's theorem (Mathlib MeasureTheory.tendstoUniformlyOn_of_ae_tendsto) there is a measurable T_j ⊆ C_j with Lⁿ(T_j) ≤ ε/2^{j+3} such that η_k → 0 uniformly on C_j ∖ T_j.
- Put A₀ := ⋃_j (C_j ∖ T_j) ⊆ C. Since C = ⋃_j C_j, we have C ∖ A₀ ⊆ ⋃_j T_j, so Lⁿ(C ∖ A₀) ≤ Σ_{j≥1} ε/2^{j+3} = ε/8.

6. (A closed A ⊆ A₀.)
- For every j, C_j ∖ T_j is measurable with finite measure. By inner regularity (MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt) there is a closed A_j ⊆ C_j ∖ T_j with Lⁿ((C_j ∖ T_j) ∖ A_j) < ε/2^{j+3}.
- Let A := ⋃_j A_j. Since A_j ⊆ C_j ⊆ S_j, A is closed by (★).
- A ⊆ A₀ ⊆ C ⊆ D and A₀ ∖ A ⊆ ⋃_j ((C_j ∖ T_j) ∖ A_j), so Lⁿ(A₀ ∖ A) ≤ ε/8.
- As ℝⁿ ∖ A ⊆ (ℝⁿ ∖ C) ∪ (C ∖ A₀) ∪ (A₀ ∖ A), we get Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ A) ≤ ε/4 + ε/8 + ε/8 = ε/2 < ε.
- Uniformity on bounded sets: suppose W ⊆ {|x| < J} with J ∈ ℕ. Then W ∩ A ⊆ ⋃_{j≤J} (C_j ∖ T_j), because A_j ⊆ S_j ⊆ {|x| > j − 1} does not meet {|x| < J} when j > J. This is a finite union of sets on each of which η_k → 0 uniformly, so η_k → 0 uniformly on W ∩ A.

7. (Whitney's hypothesis (‡) on A.)
(i) g is Lipschitz, hence continuous on A.
(ii) Dg is continuous on A ⊆ C by step 3.
(iii) Let K′ ⊆ A be compact and δ > 0. K′ is bounded, so by step 6 there is k ≥ 1 with η_k(x) ≤ δ for all x ∈ K′. Let x ∈ K′ and y ∈ A with |x − y| < 1/k. If y = x, then |g(y) − g(x) − Dg(x)(y − x)| = 0 ≤ δ|y − x|. If y ≠ x, then y ∈ C and 0 < |y − x| < 1/k, so |g(y) − g(x) − Dg(x)(y − x)| = |R(x,y)| |y − x| ≤ η_k(x)|y − x| ≤ δ|y − x|.
Hence for every compact K′ ⊆ A and δ > 0 there is ρ := 1/k > 0 such that |g(y) − g(x) − Dg(x)(y − x)| ≤ δ|y − x| for all x ∈ K′ and y ∈ A with |x − y| < ρ. This is Simon's condition 1.6 (‡) for h := g|A and τ := Dg|A. It is exactly SimonGMT's HasWhitneyC1Compatibility A g (fderiv ℝ g), with fields continuous_value, continuous_derivative and remainder.

8. (Whitney extension and conclusion.)
- By the Whitney Extension Theorem (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.6; see [EG92, §6.5], [Fed69, 3.1.14]) there is a C¹ function h : ℝⁿ → ℝ with h(a) = g(a) and HasFDerivAt h (Dg(a)) a for every a ∈ A.
- In Lean this is SimonGMT Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.exists_contDiff_one_extension_of_whitney : IsClosed A → HasWhitneyC1Compatibility A h D → ∃ g′, ContDiff ℝ 1 g′ ∧ EqOn g′ h A ∧ ∀ a ∈ A, HasFDerivAt g′ (D a) a, in Poincare/SimonGMT/Chapter02/WhitneyExtension.lean of the pinned simongmt package.

- Let x ∈ A. Then g(x) = h(x). By uniqueness of the Fréchet derivative, fderiv ℝ h x = Dg(x).
- Since x ∈ A ⊆ D, g is differentiable at x, i.e. HasFDerivAt g (Dg(x)) x, which is HasFDerivAt g (fderiv ℝ h x) x.
- Together with step 6 (A is closed and Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ A) < ε), this proves the theorem. ∎

η_k(x) := sup{|R(x,y)| : y ∈ C, 0 < |y − x| < 1/k} is bounded by 2K, decreases to 0 on C, and is Borel (lower semicontinuous on C).

subproblems.title: C¹ Lusin pieces of a real function that is Lipschitz on an open set (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5, localized)
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ (ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), Lⁿ = volume), let Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ be open, and let u : ℝⁿ → ℝ be K-Lipschitz on Ω for some K ≥ 0. Then there are C¹ functions h_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ and sets A_k ⊆ Ω (k ∈ ℕ) such that, for every k and every w ∈ A_k, u(w) = h_k(w) and u is Fréchet differentiable at w with derivative Dh_k(w) = fderiv ℝ h_k w; and Lⁿ(Ω ∖ ⋃_k A_k) = 0.

Conventions. ℝⁿ = Eucl n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Euclidean norm |·|. Lⁿ = volume (Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ). Dh(w) := fderiv ℝ h w. "u is K-Lipschitz on Ω" means |u(y) − u(z)| ≤ K|y − z| for all y, z ∈ Ω.

Source. This is Step 2 of the proof of slicing_im_st_chart_data: the C¹ Approximation Theorem (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5) applied to a McShane extension. Here it is stated for an arbitrary real function that is Lipschitz on an open set. The C¹ Approximation Theorem is the sibling c1_approximation_real (Submission.lpf_c1_approximation_real). It states: if g : ℝⁿ → ℝ is K-Lipschitz and 0 < ε ≤ ∞, then there are a closed set A ⊆ ℝⁿ with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ A) < ε and a C¹ function h : ℝⁿ → ℝ such that, for every x ∈ A, g(x) = h(x) and g has Fréchet derivative Dh(x) at x.

Let Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ be open and let u : ℝⁿ → ℝ be K-Lipschitz on Ω.

1. (McShane extension.) There is g : ℝⁿ → ℝ that is K-Lipschitz on all of ℝⁿ with g = u on Ω. For example, take g(x) := inf_{y ∈ Ω} (u(y) + K|x − y|), or g := 0 if Ω = ∅ (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_real).

2. (C¹ approximation.) For k ∈ ℕ let ε_k := 1/(k + 1) ∈ (0, 1]. Apply the sibling c1_approximation_real to g, K and ε_k. This gives a closed set C_k ⊆ ℝⁿ with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ C_k) < 1/(k + 1) and a C¹ function h_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ such that, for every x ∈ C_k, g(x) = h_k(x) and g has Fréchet derivative Dh_k(x) at x.

3. (The sets.) Put A_k := Ω ∩ C_k. Then A_k ⊆ Ω.

4. (Values and derivatives on A_k.) Let w ∈ A_k.
   - u(w) = g(w) because w ∈ Ω (step 1), and g(w) = h_k(w) because w ∈ C_k (step 2). So u(w) = h_k(w).
   - Ω is open and contains w, so u = g on the neighbourhood Ω of w. If a function agrees near w with a function that has Fréchet derivative L at w, then it also has Fréchet derivative L at w (HasFDerivAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq).
   - g has Fréchet derivative Dh_k(w) at w (step 2). Hence u has Fréchet derivative Dh_k(w) = fderiv ℝ h_k w at w.

5. (Null remainder.) Fix k ∈ ℕ.
   - If w ∈ Ω ∖ ⋃_l A_l, then w ∉ C_k; otherwise w ∈ Ω ∩ C_k = A_k. So Ω ∖ ⋃_l A_l ⊆ ℝⁿ ∖ C_k.
   - Hence Lⁿ(Ω ∖ ⋃_l A_l) ≤ Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ C_k) < 1/(k + 1).
   This holds for every k ∈ ℕ, and 1/(k + 1) → 0 as k → ∞ (ENNReal.tendsto_inv_nat_nhds_zero). Therefore Lⁿ(Ω ∖ ⋃_k A_k) = 0.

6. (Conclusion.) Steps 2–5 give the required C¹ functions h_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ and sets A_k ⊆ Ω (k ∈ ℕ):
   - for every k and every w ∈ A_k, u(w) = h_k(w) and u has Fréchet derivative fderiv ℝ h_k w at w;
   - Lⁿ(Ω ∖ ⋃_k A_k) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: McShane: extend u|Ω to a K-Lipschitz g : ℝⁿ → ℝ (LipschitzOnWith.extend_real).
Sibling c1_approximation_real with ε = 1/(k+1): closed C_k and C¹ h_k with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ C_k) < 1/(k+1), g = h_k and g has derivative Dh_k on C_k.
A_k := Ω ∩ C_k: there u = g = h_k, and since u = g on the open set Ω, u has derivative Dh_k(w) at every w ∈ A_k (HasFDerivAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq).
Ω ∖ ⋃_l A_l ⊆ ℝⁿ ∖ C_k for every k, so its Lⁿ-measure is < 1/(k+1) for all k, hence 0.

subproblems.title: Directional derivative of a Lipschitz map along DΦ(w)s equals D(f∘Φ)(w)s (Simon Ch. 2, 4.7/4.10)
subproblems.statement: Let n, P, Q ∈ ℕ, f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q, Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P and w ∈ ℝⁿ. Suppose f is K-Lipschitz (K ≥ 0) on some neighbourhood V of Φ(w), Φ is differentiable at w, and f∘Φ is differentiable at w. Then for every s ∈ ℝⁿ the map t ↦ f(Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s) (t ∈ ℝ) has derivative D(f∘Φ)(w)s at t = 0, where DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w and D(f∘Φ)(w) = fderiv ℝ (f ∘ Φ) w.

Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with norm |·|; DΦ(w) := fderiv ℝ Φ w and D(f∘Φ)(w) := fderiv ℝ (f ∘ Φ) w; “f is K-Lipschitz on V” means |f(y) − f(z)| ≤ K|y − z| for all y, z ∈ V; o(t) denotes a function of t ∈ ℝ that is little-o of t as t → 0.

This is the fact (DD) used in step 5 of the parent proof (lpf_chart_chain_rule; Simon Ch. 2, 4.7 and 4.10): for small |t| both Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s and Φ(w + ts) lie in V, so |f(Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s) − f(Φ(w + ts))| ≤ K|Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s − Φ(w + ts)| = o(t), while f(Φ(w + ts)) = f(Φ(w)) + t·D(f∘Φ)(w)s + o(t).

Fix s ∈ ℝⁿ and put x := Φ(w), v := DΦ(w)s, b := D(f∘Φ)(w)s, g₁(t) := f(x + t v), g₂(t) := f(Φ(w + t s)) and h := g₁ − g₂ (t ∈ ℝ).

1. (Derivatives along the line.) The affine line ℓ(t) := w + t s satisfies ℓ(0) = w and has derivative s at t = 0. Since Φ is differentiable at w = ℓ(0), the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt) shows that t ↦ Φ(w + t s) has derivative DΦ(w)s = v at t = 0. Since f∘Φ is differentiable at w, the chain rule likewise shows that g₂ = (f∘Φ)∘ℓ has derivative D(f∘Φ)(w)s = b at t = 0.

2. (First-order expansion of Φ along the line.) By step 1 and the little-o characterization of derivatives (hasDerivAt_iff_isLittleO), using Φ(w + 0·s) = x: Φ(w + t s) − x − t v = o(t) as t → 0.

3. (Both points eventually lie in V.) As t → 0, x + t v → x (continuity of t ↦ x + t v) and Φ(w + t s) → Φ(w) = x (the map t ↦ Φ(w + t s) is differentiable, hence continuous, at 0). Since V is a neighbourhood of x, there is a neighbourhood of t = 0 on which x + t v ∈ V and Φ(w + t s) ∈ V. For such t, because f is K-Lipschitz on V,
|h(t)| = |f(x + t v) − f(Φ(w + t s))| ≤ K|x + t v − Φ(w + t s)| = K|Φ(w + t s) − x − t v|.

4. (h has derivative 0 at 0.) By step 3, h(t) = O(|Φ(w + t s) − x − t v|) as t → 0, and by step 2 the latter is o(t); hence h(t) = o(t) (Asymptotics.IsBigO.trans_isLittleO). Moreover h(0) = f(x) − f(Φ(w)) = 0. So h(t) − h(0) − t·0 = o(t), i.e. h has derivative 0 at t = 0 (hasDerivAt_iff_isLittleO).

5. (Conclusion.) g₁ = g₂ + h pointwise, since g₂(t) + (g₁(t) − g₂(t)) = g₁(t). By steps 1 and 4 and the sum rule (HasDerivAt.add), g₁ has derivative b + 0 = b at t = 0, that is, HasDerivAt (fun t => f (Φ w + t • fderiv ℝ Φ w s)) (fderiv ℝ (f ∘ Φ) w s) 0. ∎

Φ(w + ts) − Φ(w) − t·DΦ(w)s = o(t).
For t near 0 both Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s and Φ(w + ts) lie in V, so |g₁(t) − g₂(t)| ≤ K|Φ(w + ts) − Φ(w) − t·DΦ(w)s| = o(t).
